title: Enrollment Standards for Home Protection Plans: Holdings per Premise
content:
These standards govern how many Home Protection Plans a customer may hold and which combinations may be live at one premise. A plan is **live** while its status is waiting period or active; a cancelled plan is not live.

## Standards

**Standard 1. No limit per customer.** A customer may hold Home Protection Plans at each premise they occupy, with no overall limit on the number of plans per customer.

**Standard 2. One live plan of the same name per premise.** Only one plan of the same name may be live at one premise; the per-premise limit for live plans of the same plan is 1 for every plan in the line. Whether a plan of that name is already live is decided from the company's plan records for that premise (the premise, the plan name and the plan status), as they stand before the enrollment is made.

**Standard 3. The exclusive plan.** Holding a plan whose terms exclude holding any other protection plan at the same premise (in the current line, Beacon Ridge Whole Home Shield) changes eligibility for every other plan at that premise: while it is live no other plan may be enrolled there, and it may not be enrolled while another plan is live there, because it already covers every system.

## Standards restated as conditions

| What the plan records show at the premise | Enrollment sought at that premise | Outcome under these standards |
|---|---|---|
| A live plan of the same name | Another plan of that same name | Not permitted (Standard 2) |
| A live Beacon Ridge Whole Home Shield | Any other plan | Not permitted (Standard 3) |
| Any other live plan | Beacon Ridge Whole Home Shield | Not permitted (Standard 3) |

## Illustrations (hypothetical holdings)

1. A premise holds Beacon Ridge HVAC Repair Plan in waiting period. A second Beacon Ridge HVAC Repair Plan at that premise is not permitted: a plan in waiting period is live.
2. A premise holds a cancelled Beacon Ridge HVAC Repair Plan and no other plan. Standard 2 does not stand in the way of a new Beacon Ridge HVAC Repair Plan there, because a cancelled plan is not live.
3. A customer holds Beacon Ridge Surge Shield at one home and asks for Beacon Ridge Surge Shield at a second home. Standard 2 counts plans per premise, and Standard 1 sets no limit per customer, so neither standard stands in the way.
4. A premise holds an active Beacon Ridge Home Wiring Care. Beacon Ridge Whole Home Shield may not be enrolled there while that plan is live.
5. A premise holds a live Beacon Ridge Whole Home Shield. Beacon Ridge Electric Line Guard may not be enrolled there.
